title: Module-target active operators reconstruct interval fibres and module tail
statement: Use the ordinary ordered-fibre category $\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes}$ of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. For $t\geq0$, put $X_1(t)=(\langle t\rangle,\varnothing)$ and $X_0(t)=(\langle t+1\rangle,\{t+1\})$. For a monotone map $\beta:[q]\to[p]$, where $[t]=\{0,\ldots,t\}$, define the following ordinary arrows, with each displayed fibre ordered increasingly. The arrow $T_\beta:X_1(p)\to X_1(q)$ has fibre $(\beta(i-1),\beta(i)]$ at output $1\leq i\leq q$ and discards every other input. The arrow $K_\beta:X_0(p)\to X_1(q)$ has the same fibres and discards all other inputs, including the module input. The arrow $B_\beta:X_0(p)\to X_0(q)$ has those algebra-output fibres and module-output fibre $(\beta(q),p+1]$, discarding precisely the inputs at most $\beta(0)$. Here $(u,v]$ denotes the list $u+1,\ldots,v$, empty if $u=v$. Write $D^1_\beta=T_\beta$ and $D^0_\beta=K_\beta$. Let $r,s,n\geq0$, let $\alpha:[n]\to[s]$ and $\delta:[n]\to[r]$ be monotone, with $\alpha(0)=0$. Suppose $h:X_0(r)\to X_0(s)$ is any arrow of $\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes}$ satisfying $B_\alpha\circ h=B_\delta$. Let $C_j$ be its ordered fibre at algebra output $1\leq j\leq s$, and $C_{s+1}$ its ordered module-output fibre. Define integers $\lambda(0)=\delta(0)$ and $\lambda(j)=\delta(0)+\sum_{l=1}^j|C_l|$ for $1\leq j\leq s$. Then $\lambda$ takes values in $[r]$ and is monotone, each algebra fibre $C_j$ is the increasing list $(\lambda(j-1),\lambda(j)]$, the module fibre $C_{s+1}$ is the increasing nonempty list $(\lambda(s),r+1]$ ending in the unique module input, and $\lambda\circ\alpha=\delta$. The inputs discarded by $h$ are exactly those at most $\delta(0)$. In particular $h=B_\lambda$. These conclusions include $s=0$, $n=0$ and empty algebra-output fibres.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 4.1.2.11, final cartesian-lift calculation; Remark 4.2.2.8, left-module analogue. Agent expansion of the ordered-fibre calculation; no Stacks tag covers this operator-combinatorial assertion. WANTED archive in literature/.

proof.text:
The arrows displayed in the statement are legitimate ordered-fibre arrows: each algebra-output fibre contains only algebra inputs; the module-output fibre of $B_\beta$ contains the unique module input $p+1$, last, since $\beta(q)\leq p$. By [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding], composition substitutes fibres in their specified outer order. Write $F_i$ for the ordered fibre of $B_\alpha\circ h$ at algebra output $i$, and $F_m$ for its module-output fibre. Thus, writing $\Vert$ for concatenation, for $1\leq i\leq n$ and for the module output respectively,
$$F_i=C_{\alpha(i-1)+1}\Vert\cdots\Vert C_{\alpha(i)},\qquad F_m=C_{\alpha(n)+1}\Vert\cdots\Vert C_{s+1}.$$
Empty ranges contribute empty lists. Equality with $B_\delta$ gives $F_i=(\delta(i-1),\delta(i)]$ and $F_m=(\delta(n),r+1]$ as ordered lists.

proof.text:
Because $\alpha(0)=0$, the ranges in step 1, followed by the module range, traverse every index $1,\ldots,s+1$ exactly once, in order. Concatenating their equalities therefore gives
$$C_1\Vert\cdots\Vert C_{s+1}=(\delta(0),r+1].$$
The right side has no gaps or repetitions and has its increasing order. Hence its entries, and only those entries, occur in non-basepoint fibres of $h$. Every remaining non-basepoint input is sent to the basepoint, so the inputs discarded by $h$ are exactly $1,\ldots,\delta(0)$. This also proves that no retained input is lost in the second arrow; that conclusion uses the initial endpoint condition, not a terminal endpoint condition.

proof.text:
Put $a_j=\sum_{l=1}^j|C_l|$ for $0\leq j\leq s$, with $a_0=0$. In the list equality of step 2, the entries of $C_j$ occupy precisely positions $a_{j-1}+1,\ldots,a_j$. The entry in position $k$ of its right side is $\delta(0)+k$. Consequently
$$C_j=(\delta(0)+a_{j-1},\delta(0)+a_j]=(\lambda(j-1),\lambda(j)]\quad(1\leq j\leq s).$$
The remaining positions form $C_{s+1}$, so $C_{s+1}=(\delta(0)+a_s,r+1]=(\lambda(s),r+1]$. These are identities of ordered lists, since positions record order as well as entries; they also hold when $a_j=a_{j-1}$.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Notation 4.2.1.6, Construction 4.2.2.6 and Remark 4.2.2.8; expansion of the final cartesian-lift calculation of Proposition 4.1.2.11. proof.text:
The module-fibre condition in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding] says that $C_{s+1}$ contains exactly the unique module input $r+1$, last. In particular $|C_{s+1}|\geq1$. Taking lengths in step 2 gives
$$\delta(0)+a_s=r+1-|C_{s+1}|\leq r.$$
Since $\delta(0)\geq0$ and every summand in $a_j$ is nonnegative, $0\leq\lambda(0)\leq\cdots\leq\lambda(s)\leq r$. Thus the specified integers define a monotone map $[s]\to[r]$. The formula in step 3 for the final fibre is a nonempty increasing list ending in $r+1$.

proof.text:
For $0\leq i\leq n$, the first $i$ algebra-output fibres in step 1 concatenate to $C_1\Vert\cdots\Vert C_{\alpha(i)}$: for $i=0$ both lists are empty because $\alpha(0)=0$. Their $B_\delta$ expressions concatenate to $(\delta(0),\delta(i)]$. Counting entries yields
$$\sum_{l=1}^{\alpha(i)}|C_l|=\delta(i)-\delta(0).$$
Adding $\delta(0)$ gives $\lambda(\alpha(i))=\delta(i)$ for every $i$, including $i=0$. Therefore $\lambda\circ\alpha=\delta$. No argument uses $\alpha(n)=s$: the unused algebra outputs after $\alpha(n)$ occur in $F_m$.

proof.text: Steps 2 and 3 identify every ordered non-basepoint fibre and every discarded input of $h$ with those defining $B_\lambda$. A morphism in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding] consists exactly of its pointed map and these fibre orders, so $h=B_\lambda$. For $s=0$, step 2 says $C_1=(\delta(0),r+1]$ and step 5 forces $\delta(i)=\delta(0)$, as required. For $n=0$, step 1 has just its module equality, which is already the full list equality used in steps 2–4; step 5 reduces to $\lambda(0)=\delta(0)$. Empty algebra fibres give equal consecutive values of $\lambda$, so require no strict-monotonicity hypothesis.
